transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15 10:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Rachel Moore (Head of Search, Igneous), Devon Park (ML Engineer), Asha Iyer (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on embeddings + rerank. Customer has existing OpenSearch + Pinecone eval for vectors, wants lower latency at scale and better recall for long-doc QA.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samir from Redwood, and Leah our solutions eng is here too. Quick intros?
[00:10] Rachel: Hi Samir, Rachel here. We run search for Igneous's knowledge base and product docs. We're exploring embeddings + rerank to improve relevancy for long queries.
[00:20] Devon: Devon, ML infra. I mostly own the vector infra and the pipeline. Right now we use Pinecone for vectors and OpenSearch for inverted index.
[00:28] Leah: Great, thanks. Asha?
[00:30] Asha: Asha, CTO. I'll be on some calls; main question is cost vs performance and security side.

[00:45] Samir: Cool. So quick context checks: what's your current qps, average doc length, and embedding dims?
[00:53] Devon: We're doing around 150 qps peak, typical queries 200-800 tokens returned; docs chunked at 1k tokens. Embedding dim is 768 for our current model (we're using a 768-d sim model). Storage is getting expensive.
[01:10] Leah: Okay 150 qps peak, 768 dims — that maps to storage and compute. Are you doing hybrid search now? BM25 pre-filter + vector rerank?
[01:18] Devon: Yes, BM25 -> top 200 -> vector re-rank with Pinecone approximate NN (HNSW). Latency is about 250-300ms on average but spikes to 700ms during bursts.
[01:28] Rachel: Those spikes are painful — search is part of UX. We want median <200ms and 95th <400ms.
[01:35] Samir: Understood. Two levers: index architecture and the inference path for reranking. For rerank, are you doing cross-encoder scoring or just dot-product between query and doc embeddings?
[01:45] Devon: Right now it's dot-product for candidate scoring, we then run a small cross-encoder for top-5 rerank which is the heaviest part.
[01:54] Leah: Got it. So if the heavy cross-encoder is in the critical path, Dedicated capacity helps because you can provision GPUs for low-latency cross-encoder runs. Hosted may also handle it but you'd need to check concurrency and burst policies.
[02:06] Asha: Can you explain the difference in fallback? Like, what happens if hosted region is saturated?
[02:12] Samir: We have smart routing and fallbacks. For hosted, requests can fall back to a cheaper model or to a cached response. For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput. Private gives you full control with VPC and KMS.
[02:24] Devon: Any friction integrating with our existing Pinecone index? We don't want to reindex.
[02:30] Leah: Absolutely. Many customers keep Pinecone or Milvus and use Redwood for the rerank step only. You can either call Redwood to generate embeddings (and push them to your index) or you can keep your embeddings and send candidates to Redwood for cross-encoder scoring. We support batched scoring APIs and streaming.
[02:46] Rachel: Are there API examples for hybrid search pipelines?
[02:50] Samir: Yes — we'll share a sample pipeline doc. We'll include the BM25+ANN candidate flow and recommended batch sizes.

[03:05] Devon: About embedding dim: could we reduce from 768 to 256 or 128 to save storage? Any loss in quality?
[03:12] Leah: There's usually a tradeoff. For semantic recall, 256 often works fine for many datasets; 128 can be okay for narrow domains. We also recommend projection or training a small transformation layer so you retain performance. Redwood Optimize gives quantization and dimensionality guidance per workload.
[03:28] Rachel: What about ANN indexes? We use HNSW today. Does Redwood recommend a different approach?
[03:33] Leah: HNSW is solid. For very high write volume or sharded setups, IVF+PQ might be cheaper but increases recall variance. If you want fewer false negatives on large corpora, HNSW is common.
[03:44] Devon: Any best practices for chunking?
[03:46] Leah: Keep chunks semantically coherent — 500-1k tokens is common. For rerank, larger chunks can help recall but costs more compute during rerank.

[04:05] Asha: Security question: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS. Also some customers require data residency in EU.
[04:14] Samir: We have SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integrations — we'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 cert. For residency, Hosted has region controls; Private is recommended if you need on-prem or air-gapped.
[04:28] Devon: If we go Dedicated, how do upgrades and rollouts work? We don't want downtime during canary or patching.
[04:35] Leah: Dedicated supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback. The control plane will orchestrate model version pinning; traffic can be routed by percent during canaries. And the runtime supports graceful degradation (fallback to a smaller cross-encoder) if needed.
[04:52] Rachel: Pricing: how do you price reranking? Is it per token or per request/embedding call?
[04:58] Samir: Hosted usage-based: per-token for generation/cross-encoder calls and per-embedding unit for embeddings. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) — typically cheaper for sustained high qps. We'll send detailed pricing sheets.

[05:15] Devon: For the benchmark, we want to test 150 qps sustained and bursts to 400 qps. Can you support that load on Hosted?
[05:23] Leah: Hosted can handle bursts but it depends on concurrency and model choice; for consistent 400 qps with low 95th latency, Dedicated is usually the better fit. We can run a benchmark on Hosted to quantify.
[05:34] Samir: Action: we'll run a 2-hour benchmark with your sample dataset and measure median/95th latency for both Hosted and a Dedicated simulator.
[05:41] Devon: Great. We'll provide a 10k doc sample with current embeddings and OpenSearch candidate flow.

[06:00] Rachel: A practical point — we use a mixture of exact match boost plus semantic rank. How smooth is tuning?
[06:07] Leah: We expose scoring weights and you can do hybrid scoring on the client side too. Redwood Console shows token-level cost and latency and can surface quality regressions for prompt changes.
[06:20] Asha: Contracts — if we go Dedicated, what's the typical commit? 6 or 12 months?
[06:26] Samir: Most customers do 12-months for Dedicated but we have 6-month pilot options. We'll map pricing to qps and expected token volume.

[06:40] Devon: Any known gotchas when integrating with Pinecone? Rate limits?
[06:44] Leah: Usually the main friction is synchronous calls causing latency because candidate fetching is network-bound. We recommend async prefetching and caching of top candidates where possible. Also, align your ANN shards to minimize cross-node scatter.

[07:05] Rachel: Can Redwood host embeddings for us and then host the ANN index — basically move us off Pinecone?
[07:10] Samir: Yes, we can host embeddings and run vector indexes for you in Hosted or Dedicated. That reduces latency between embedding generation and indexing. We'll share migration guidance.

[07:30] Devon: For cross-encoder model size — what do customers typically use for rerank? small bi-encoder vs full cross-encoder?
[07:37] Leah: Many do a two-stage: bi-encoder dot-product for recall, then a lightweight cross-encoder for top-n (e.g., rerank with a distilled cross-encoder). This keeps cost down and latencies acceptable. If you need high precision, a larger cross-encoder helps but increases latency.

[08:05] Samir: Quick note — we mentioned 'KV cache' earlier, sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in our logs — but that's the runtime cache for autoregressive models, doesn't apply much to rerank flows which are encoder-only.

[08:20] Rachel: Okay, let's talk timeline. We're aiming for a pilot in Q3, production by Q4 if results are good. Key stakeholders: CTO (Asha), Head of Search (Rachel), ML infra (Devon).
[08:30] Samir: Sounds good. We'll prepare a benchmark plan and a pricing options doc.

[08:40] Leah: I'll also draft a recommended architecture: keep OpenSearch as the BM25 prefilter, keep your Pinecone or migrate to Redwood-hosted index depending on results, use a 256-d projection experiment to compare storage and recall, and run cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated for latency-sensitive traffic.

[08:58] Devon: If we do 256 dims, what's the expected storage reduction?
[09:02] Leah: Roughly 33% compared to 768 -> 512 -> 256. Also you can apply quantization (int8 or 4-bit) to save another ~50-75% depending on technique. Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles.

[09:20] Asha: Any red flags for compliance? If we go Hosted, can data be locked to EU region?
[09:25] Samir: Hosted region controls are available and we can restrict residency. For stricter controls we'd recommend Private deployment. We'll include the region/residency doc.

[09:40] Rachel: Great. Before we close, one more thing: can you share an example notebook that wires Pinecone -> Redwood rerank?
[09:46] Samir: Yes, we'll attach a quickstart notebook and a sample benchmark harness.

[10:00] (recap) Samir: Recap: Samir to send pricing and Hosted vs Dedicated guide; Leah to prepare benchmark plan and sample architecture; Devon to share sample data and vector schema; schedule the benchmark next week.
[10:12] Rachel: Thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[10:15] Asha: Thanks.

End of transcript.
